clue.text: Work on a new look — continue appearing in shot, getting good in certain lines

indicators.note: something appearing in a picture is placed within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a shot is a photograph, a pic
to continue is to last

indicators.note: the good letter is set in the middle of the word for certain

parts.note: certain means sure
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A makeover story: someone keeps turning up in photos and behaving well in particular rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' and 'in' are both containment signals; 'getting' is only a link. RY for railway lines is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic operations are performed to give a patient a changed appearance.

clue.text: Character in series displaying power, enhancing northern show

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
enhancing something is adding to it
to bear is to show, as in bearing marks or a likeness

explanation.surface: A TV series character shows strength, adding to a show from the North of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The bear from Peru stars in a long run of Michael Bond children's books and their screen adaptations.

clue.text: Ways gunmen raised weapons

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Gunmen lift their guns in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards, so the whole charade is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store or collection of arms, so it stands for weapons collectively.

clue.text: Malt whisky confusing to man clutching old whiskey label

indicators.note: read playfully as whisked, the word tells us to stir up the letters of the word beside it
the jumbled words to man hold the old and whiskey letters within them
confusing letters jumbles them into a new order

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Malt whisky bewilders a man holding an old whiskey label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisky' is read as whisked, an anagram signal for the word before it; 'confusing' jumbles TO MAN as AMOTN, and 'clutching' puts OW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamla Motown was the record company (record label) behind the Detroit soul sound.

clue.text: Issue about a new projection

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for issue goes round the other letters

parts.note: a copy is an issue of a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: A publication about a fresh plan or forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhanging cover that juts out from a building, a projection.

clue.text: November in American harbour is rather hairy

indicators.note: the November letter is placed in the word for American

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a haven is a harbour

explanation.surface: A US port in November looks somewhat shaggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshaven has stubble, so their face is somewhat hairy.

clue.text: Region of India not Liberal in ambition

indicators.note: not here means the Liberal letter is left out of the word for ambition

parts.note: a goal is an ambition

explanation.surface: A part of India where the Liberals have no aspirations.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on India's west coast, formerly Portuguese.

clue.text: Have third thoughts about defensive structure?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to doubt again, and doubts are second thoughts, so a further round is third thoughts

explanation.surface: Reconsidering yet again whether a fort is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense invents a verb: doubting something is having second thoughts, so doubting it again is third thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is an enclosed outwork or stronghold, a fortification held by defenders.

clue.text: Armies move easily around Spain, uplifting the historic catering supplier

indicators.note: the word for armies goes around the Spain letter

parts.note: hosts are armies, as in the heavenly host
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to stroll is to walk at ease

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting reads the old word for the backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: Troops wander around Spain while a historic supplier of food lifts their spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses the archaic article, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess trolley is a heated serving cart that keeps dishes warm, a 1970s dinner-party fixture.

clue.text: Collector in greyish-brown carrying amounts around

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the colour word contains the other piece

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: around here turns the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: AMTS is a standard abbreviation for amounts

explanation.surface: A collector dressed in drab brown carries sums about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the abbreviation before the colour word holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman is a British refuse collector who empties household bins.

clue.text: An opening for dramatics claimed by average awkward person

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into it, so the average word holds the rest

parts.note: so-so means average

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so this takes the first letter of dramatics

explanation.surface: An average performer lands a part in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a euphemism for an annoying or difficult individual.

clue.text: No specific number entertained by popular hostelry

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so the popular word holds the letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An unknown crowd welcomed at a well-liked pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or small hotel, which is what a hostelry is.

clue.text: Attraction leading to attempt to marry? Legal intervention here

parts.note: appeal is attraction or charm
to court someone is to woo them in hope of marriage

explanation.surface: Attraction leads to a proposal, and the lawyers step in.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges in a higher tribunal step in to overturn or uphold lower decisions, so legal intervention happens there.

clue.text: Concern about profits almost entirely seen in marketplace?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for concern goes round the rest

parts.note: care is concern
boots is an old word for profits or advantages, as in to boot

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Worry over whether earnings are nearly all visible in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is an outdoor sale where people sell goods from car boots (car trunks), an impromptu market.

clue.text: Race completely in control of Republicans

indicators.note: a word in control of another holds it, so the Republicans' letters go around the rest

parts.note: the GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
all means completely

explanation.surface: A race run entirely by the Republican Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop is to run fast, as a horse does, so it can mean race as a verb.

clue.text: Remains bored, withdrawing our team's boxing debut at last

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the reversed letters wrap round the last of debut
withdrawing means pulling back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: tired means bored, as in tired of it

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of debut

parts.note: us is our team, said of ourselves

explanation.surface: Our team was bored and pulled out, a boxer making a debut at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' reverses only the word for bored; 'boxing' then puts the final letter of debut inside, and 'at last' picks that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or leftover waste, what remains after something breaks up.

clue.text: Elevated speech from founder, losing one argument

indicators.note: losing means the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: to founder is to fail
I is the Roman numeral one
a set-to is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A high-pitched voice comes from a company founder who loses an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a man's voice raised above its natural range, so the speech is pitched high.

clue.text: Voluntary work involving keys will engross island

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: to engross is to absorb, so the music word takes in the island letter

parts.note: tonal music is written in keys

explanation.surface: Unpaid work playing the keyboard on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is a matter of choice, as voluntary acts are.

clue.text: Someone complaining in manner having weight

indicators.note: the complainer goes in the word for manner

parts.note: tone is manner, as in the tone of a remark
a nag is someone who keeps complaining

explanation.surface: A moaner whose style carries real heft.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures the weight or carrying capacity of a ship or cargo.

clue.text: Officer of the law rejected loophole

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
out means rejected, as in that plan is out

explanation.surface: A policeman turns down a legal escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion of responsibility, so it works like an escape clause.

clue.text: Excluded over infiltrating organisation

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the over letter goes into the organisation word

parts.note: an outfit is an organisation or firm
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Kept out after getting inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of it is being left out or not part of things.

clue.text: A sign restricting parking repeatedly in Middle East city

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so A and the sign hold the parking letters

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: repeatedly gives the parking letter twice

parts.note: P is the sign and abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A sign that limits parking again and again in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, in the Middle East.

clue.text: Crazy suggestion backed eating large dessert

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the backed word holds the large letter
backed means turned back to front

parts.note: a tip is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A mad idea to turn back after eating a big pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is an ice-cream sundae built on a halved banana, a pudding.

clue.text: Couple and haul, moving weight forwards

indicators.note: moving means a letter is shifted to another place in the word
forwards says the weight letter goes towards the front

parts.note: to tow is to haul

explanation.surface: A pair hauling, shifting weight to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, and a pair numbers exactly that many things.

clue.text: A little taken aback, interrupted by chap refusing to back down?

indicators.note: a word interrupted by another has it inserted in the middle
taken aback reads as taken backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Slightly startled when a man cuts in who will not give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reverses only the word for little; 'interrupted by' then splits it with the chap. The A stays where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An adamant person is unyielding, standing firm rather than retreating.

clue.text: Sum? Am splitting final figure

indicators.note: taking the last Roman numeral of the word and splitting it into two equal halves, as a thousand is two five hundreds

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's question about splitting a final number.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals: M is 1000, and halving it gives D (500) twice, so A M becomes A D D.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to sum, to total up numbers, here as a verb.

clue.text: Piano melody, getting loud, starts to unwind later in high-spirited style

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a lay is a song or melody in poetry
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A tune on the piano grows loud before winding down later in lively fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful means lively and full of fun, the spirit of something done light-heartedly.

clue.text: Refuse to associate with second attempt securing expulsion of witches?

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the outer pieces enclose the phrase

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end to a coven, the gathering of witches, read as a phrase

explanation.surface: A second go at banishing a coven of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise someone, to shun them by not speaking, is the idiom's meaning.
